clue.text: Another peculation from Mary Wesley?

definitions.note: a novel by Mary Wesley, standing for its title

parts.note: another one, coming after the first, is the second
peculation is embezzlement, a swindle or fiddle

explanation.surface: A literary query about yet another embezzlement in a Mary Wesley novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as fraud, but Mary Wesley wrote a novel with this title; the wordplay is simply 'another' plus 'peculation'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Wesley's 1988 novel carries this title, and the phrase also means a subordinate role.

clue.text: English leave framework for satirical poet

indicators.note: the word English is told to depart, so its letter goes out of the framework word

parts.note: a skeleton is a supporting framework

explanation.surface: An Englishman quits a structure to become a satirist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' takes E (English) out of SKELETON. John Skelton was a Tudor poet famous for biting satire.
explanation.definitionFit: John Skelton, tutor to the young Henry VIII, wrote satirical verse such as Colin Clout.

clue.text: Traditionally inscrutable, like Rumer Godden's puzzle

definitions.meaning: the stock Western cliche of an unreadable Oriental face
Rumer Godden wrote a novel titled with this word plus 'Puzzle'

explanation.definitionFit: The cliche of the impassive East supplies one sense; Godden's 1936 novel Chinese Puzzle gives the other.

clue.text: A dream of C. S. Forester

definitions.meaning: a bad dream, a terrifying vision in sleep
C. S. Forester published a story collection with this title

explanation.definitionFit: A frightening dream is one sense; Forester's collection The Nightmare supplies the bookish second.

clue.text: Marryat's candid eponymous hero

parts.note: Captain Marryat's naval novel is named after its hero Mildmay, whose first name also means honest and outspoken

explanation.definitionFit: Marryat's Frank Mildmay is the title hero, and his first name is a synonym for candid.

clue.text: Associated with the best by Leslie Thomas

definitions.text: Associated with the best by Leslie Thomas

parts.words: Associated with the best by Leslie Thomas
parts.note: Leslie Thomas wrote a novel whose title pairs this word with 'and the Best'

explanation.definitionFit: Leslie Thomas's novel Dearest and the Best links the superlative of dear to 'the best'.

clue.text: Tall fee obtained from short written work

indicators.note: the answer is got out of these letters by rearranging them, so they are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A hefty fee charged for a brief piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obtained from' asks for TALLFEE to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a printed sheet or small pamphlet, a brief piece of writing.

clue.text: A date with David Benedictus

definitions.meaning: a day in the calendar, in early summer
David Benedictus's first novel, set at Eton, has this title

explanation.definitionFit: It is a calendar day, Eton's celebration day, and the title of Benedictus's 1962 novel.

clue.text: Chance offered by Ngaio Marsh at night

definitions.meaning: Ngaio Marsh's theatrical mystery is titled with this word followed by 'Night'

explanation.definitionFit: An opening is an opportunity, and Marsh's novel Opening Night is set in a theatre.

clue.text: Bede worker is unyielding

parts.note: George Eliot's novel Adam Bede, so Bede supplies its hero's first name
a worker is a worker ant in crossword convention

explanation.surface: A monk's labourer refuses to budge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bede' looks like the Venerable Bede, but it is George Eliot's Adam Bede, giving his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means immovable or inflexible in one's resolve.

clue.text: May Sinclair's Chekhovian siblings

parts.note: May Sinclair wrote a novel sharing its title with Chekhov's play about the Prozorov girls

explanation.definitionFit: Both Sinclair's 1914 novel and Chekhov's play bear this title about a trio of sisters.

clue.text: Forrest Reid's hideaway

definitions.meaning: Forrest Reid wrote a novel with this title in his Tom Barber sequence

explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a quiet refuge, and Reid's The Retreat is a Tom Barber novel.

clue.text: Portrait painter who rang the bell?

definitions.meaning: Sir Godfrey, court portraitist to several British monarchs
one who tolls a funeral bell, knelling it

explanation.definitionFit: Godfrey Kneller painted royal portraits; a knell is a tolled bell, so one who knells rings it.

clue.text: Novel knight, or peasant, say?

indicators.note: the solver is to speak the peasant word and hear the name it makes

parts.note: a hind is an old word for a farm labourer

explanation.surface: Is this storybook knight really a peasant?
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hinde, the novelist, was a baronet, Sir Thomas Chitty, so the 'knight' is a titled writer, not a character.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hinde was the pen name of Sir Thomas Chitty, a novelist holding a baronetcy.

clue.text: French nobleman let out Greek philosopher

parts.note: an aristo is an aristocrat, the word used for French nobles of the Revolution

indicators.note: out signals the following word is disordered, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A French noble releases a Greek thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let out' reads as releasing someone, but 'out' is the anagram signal working on the three letters of 'let'; 'aristo' is the clipped word for an aristocrat, used of French nobles in the Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the Stagirite philosopher, Plato's pupil.

clue.text: "Good are invariably ungrammatical" (Oscar Wilde)

parts.note: the quotation has a gap after Good: Wilde wrote that good aims of this kind are invariably ungrammatical

explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's line in The Critic as Artist is 'Good intentions are invariably ungrammatical', so the missing word fills the gap.

clue.text: Translation of Fraser oft attributed to Francis Brett Young

indicators.note: a translation renders words in another form, so the letters are rendered into a new order

explanation.surface: A rendering of someone called Fraser credited to a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translation of' rearranges FRASEROFT. Francis Brett Young wrote the novel Far Forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Far Forest is Francis Brett Young's 1936 novel set in the Worcestershire woodland.

clue.text: Composer decomposed (or is sin)

indicators.note: decomposed means broken up, so the bracketed words are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A composer is decomposed, or is that a sin?
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini wrote operas such as The Barber of Seville.

clue.text: Floor at Orsino's court taken partly for speakers

indicators.note: only part of the run of words is taken, so the answer sits inside them

explanation.surface: In Orsino's court in Twelfth Night, the floor is given over to speakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken partly' takes letters from inside 'Floor at Orsino's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Orators are public speakers.

clue.text: Goddesses' foundations?

parts.note: foundations as underwear: the girdle worn by Venus in myth, here in the plural

explanation.definitionFit: A cestus is the girdle of Venus, so goddesses' girdles are their foundation garments.

clue.text: Falstaff went away as if he had been such a child, said the Hostess

definitions.text: Falstaff went away as if he had been such a child, said the Hostess

parts.words: Falstaff went away as if he had been such a child, said the Hostess
parts.note: in Henry V Mistress Quickly says Falstaff died like an innocent infant in its baptismal robe

explanation.definitionFit: The Hostess says he went away 'an it had been any christom child', a newly baptised infant.

clue.text: American novelist detained among offspring

indicators.note: among places the one word in the midst of the other

explanation.surface: A writer kept in custody among the children.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidney Sheldon was an American author of bestselling thrillers.

clue.text: Situation for superior actor?

parts.note: the back of the stage, where an actor stands to draw attention and outshine others

explanation.definitionFit: The rear of the stage is the position from which an actor steals the scene from colleagues.

clue.text: A few points off direction of Hamlet's madness, in short

definitions.text: A few points off direction of Hamlet's madness, in short

parts.words: A few points off direction of Hamlet's madness, in short
parts.note: Hamlet is 'but mad north-north-west'; the compass point one notch away, written in its shortened sailor's form

explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's madness is north-north-west, a couple of compass points from north-west, whose clipped form is used here.

clue.text: Their decision comes last, so they say

definitions.text: Their decision comes last, so they say

parts.words: Their decision comes last, so they say
parts.note: competition rules say the decision of the people in charge of a publication is final

explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper competitions declare that the editor's decision is final.

clue.text: Cyril Connolly's Thin Man?

parts.note: Connolly wrote that imprisoned in every fat man a thin one is wildly signalling to be let out

explanation.definitionFit: Connolly's thin man is locked within every fat man, someone on the inside.
